headline: Lumentum's chief executive says the company's optical parts for AI data centres are sold out through early 2029.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a clear supply-limit signal from a major supplier, though it is the company's own claim.
importance_line: It points to optical data links as a bottleneck that may slow AI data-centre builds, but it is the chief executive's own statement and the article reports no independent check.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by The Japan Times, that Lumentum chief executive Michael Hurlston said in a Tokyo interview on 9 Oct 2026 that the Nvidia-backed maker of optical components for fast data links is unable to meet about 70% of demand for some products through next year and 30% for others through 2028. Six months ago he said the company was on track to sell out its capacity by 2028, and analysts on average expect its sales to more than double this year.
notes: Bloomberg page is behind a bot wall (403); text read in The Japan Times, which carries the Bloomberg story and credits it.
